ONLINE ACCESS: The Tentative Agenda is generally available the Friday before the meeting. The video of the meeting is usually available to watch live during the meeting. Minutes with adopted resolutions are available 1 to 2 days after the meeting. A full copy of the minutes, agenda and meeting video can be viewed on the official Town of Southold website. If you would like help navigating the site, please feel free to call my office 631-765-1800. The meeting will be accessible in person and via Zoom and streamed live on the Town’s website. A recording of the meeting will also air on Channel 1310 and will be posted on the Town’s website. Instructions and link to attend the meeting will be available on the Town’s website or by calling the Town Clerk’s office at (631)765-1800. A telephone number will also be provided to allow members of the public to attend via telephone. Written comments and/or questions may also be submitted via email to the Town Clerk at denisn@southoldtownny.gov. Resolutions and Proposals by Town Board Members: 231-2026 A Resolution to Approve Special Meeting Minutes WHEREAS, the minutes of Town Board meetings, as provided in §106 of Article 7 of the New York Public Officers Law, shall be approved by the Board prior to them being finalized, deemed official and disseminated to the public by the Town Clerk; and WHEREAS, that the minutes of the Town’s Special Meeting held on October 1, 2026 have been presented; and WHEREAS, the Town Board has reviewed these minutes and any necessary corrections have been made; now, therefore, be it RESOLVED, that the minutes of the Town’s Special Meeting held on October 1, 2026 are hereby approved as submitted. 1 The foregoing resolution was duly moved by Councilor McHugh and seconded by Councilor Koenig and brought to a vote resulting as follows: Councilor J. McHugh VOTED: Councilor L. Koenig VOTED: Supervisor J. Conway VOTED: Councilor H. Kennedy VOTED: Councilor R. Matters VOTED: 232-2026 A Resolution to Approve the Public Hearing Meeting Minutes WHEREAS, the minutes of Town Board meetings, as provided in §106 of Article 7 of the New York Public Officers Law, shall be approved by the Board prior to them being finalized, deemed official and disseminated to the public by the Town Clerk; and WHEREAS, that the minutes of the Town’s Public Hearing Meeting held on October 14, 2026 have been presented; and WHEREAS, the Town Board has reviewed these minutes and any necessary corrections have been made; now, therefore, be it RESOLVED, that the minutes of the Town’s Public Hearing Meeting held on October 14, 2026 are hereby approved as submitted. The foregoing resolution was duly moved by Councilor McHugh and seconded by Councilor Koenig and brought to a vote resulting as follows: Councilor J. McHugh VOTED: Councilor L. Koenig VOTED: Supervisor J. Conway VOTED: Councilor H. Kennedy VOTED: Councilor R. Matters VOTED: 233-2026 A Resolution Recognizing November as “Men’s Health Awareness Month” WHEREAS, “Movember” is an annual campaign that runs throughout the month of November involving the growing of mustaches to "change the face" of men’s health and raise awareness of men’s health issues, such as prostate cancer, testicular cancer, mental health issues, and suicide prevention; and WHEREAS, significant numbers of male-related health problems could be detected and treated if men’s awareness of these problems was more pervasive. By encouraging men to get involved, Movember aims to increase early cancer detection, diagnosis, effective treatments, and ultimately reduce the number of preventable deaths; and WHEREAS, men who are educated about the value that preventive health can play in prolonging their lifespan and their role as productive family members will be more likely to participate in health screenings; now, therefore, be it RESOLVED, that the Town of East Greenbush wishes to support Men’s Health Awareness Month by raising awareness of the dangers of men’s health issues; and be it further RESOLVED, that the Town Board declares November to be Men’s Health Awareness Month in the Town of East Greenbush. 2 This resolution was duly moved by Councilor McHugh and seconded by Supervisor Conway and brought to a vote as follows: Councilor J. McHugh VOTED: Supervisor J. Conway VOTED: Councilor H. Kennedy VOTED: Councilor R. Matters VOTED: Councilor L. Koenig VOTED: 234-2026 A Resolution to Authorize a Public Auction of Surplus Equipment WHEREAS, the Town Board of the Town of East Greenbush, County of Rensselaer, State of New York has received a request from the Chief of Police to declare the following equipment as surplus; and WHEREAS, said equipment includes Obsolete Radio Equipment: WHEREAS, the amortization rate of said equipment has far exceeded its life span and is obsolete and is not suited for other departments in Town; and WHEREAS, the Director of Finance confirms that this resolution will not have a material impact on the Town’s finances; now, therefore, be it RESOLVED that the equipment listed is hereby declared as surplus; and be it further RESOLVED that the Purchasing Agent is authorized to dispose of said surplus equipment now owned by and in the custody of the East Greenbush Police Department to Algonquin Communications in exchange for services provided including inventory and memory wiping of all radios. The foregoing resolution was duly moved by Councilor McHugh and seconded by Councilor Koenig and brought to a vote resulting as follows: Councilor J. McHugh VOTED: Councilor L. Koenig VOTED: Supervisor J. Conway VOTED: Councilor H. Kennedy VOTED: Councilor R. Matters VOTED: 235-2026 A Resolution to Amend Resolution 245-2025 WHEREAS, the Town Board approved Resolution 245-2025 – approving Troy Industrial to do necessary repairs at the Transfer Station to the Trash Compactor in the amount of $23,722.17; and WHEREAS, the amount that was stated in the resolution inadvertently missed the Freight Charge of $995 which needs to be updated; and WHEREAS, Resolution 245-2025 should be updated to include the following amounts: Field Service Repair Work: $23,722.17 Freight Charge: $995.00 Total Cost: $24,717.17 ; and WHEREAS, the Director of Finance confirms that this cost can be covered by the 2026 Budget for the Transfer Station 01.8160.4; 3 now, therefore, be it RESOLVED, that the Town Board does hereby approve the amendment of Resolution 245-2025 to include the Freight Charge at $995.00 for a total cost of $24,717.17. The foregoing resolution was duly moved by Supervisor Conway and seconded by Councilor Kennedy and brought to a vote resulting as follows: Supervisor J. Conway VOTED: Councilor H. Kennedy VOTED: Councilor R. Matters VOTED: Councilor J. McHugh VOTED: Councilor L. Koenig VOTED: 236-2026 A Resolution Accepting the Resignation of Trevor Cavagnaro as Auto Mechanic in the Highway Department WHEREAS, Trevor Cavagnaro began his position as Auto Mechanic with the East Greenbush Department of Public Works Highway Department in January 2026 and has provided knowledge and skills that are essential to the daily operations of the Mechanics of DPW; and WHEREAS, on Friday, October 30th, 2026, Trevor submitted his resignation to the Commissioner of Public Works, effective Friday, November 13, 2026; and WHEREAS, the office of Public Works Administration would like to thank Trevor for his time and dedication to his position as Auto Mechanic – acknowledging that we would never hold anyone back from bettering themselves and their true potential, we wish Trevor luck in his future endeavors; and WHEREAS, Trevor leaves his position in good standing; and WHEREAS, the Director of Finance confirms that this resolution will not have an impact on the Town’s Finances, now therefore, be it RESOLVED, that the Town Board does hereby accept the resignation of Trevor Cavagnaro as Auto Mechanic with the Department of Public Works. The foregoing resolution was duly moved by Councilor Koenig and seconded by Supervisor Conway and brought to a vote resulting as follows: Councilor L. Koenig VOTED: Supervisor J. Conway VOTED: Councilor H. Kennedy VOTED: Councilor R. Matters VOTED: Councilor J. McHugh VOTED: 237-2026 A Resolution Authorizing Additional Slip Lining at 9 Park Drive WHEREAS, the Commissioner of Public Works has identified a section of pipe that requires slip lining to address concerns; and WHEREAS, the Department of Public Works has utilized the Storm Sewer slip lining budget allocation and is requesting as an additional $15,387.50 to slip line 125 Linear Feet of 12 inch pipe; and WHEREAS, the problem with this section was identified during a recent water break when the volume of water going through the storm sewer system from Point View Drive caused water to start to back up at 9 Park Drive – a residence that has experienced severe flooding issues 4 during high volume rain events and it is our hope that this can help reduce the flooding events while we continue to work on the storm sewer system and potential long term fixes; and WHEREAS, the Director of Finance confirms that the use of Sewer fund balance in the amount $15,387.50 to 07.8140.4 Storm Sewer CE to allow for the slip lining at 9 Park Drive; now, therefore, be it RESOLVED, that the Town Board doe hereby approve the use of fund balance to transfer $15,387.50 to 07.8140.4 Storm Sewer CE to allow for 9 Park Drive slip lining of 12” pipe at 125 Linear Feet. The foregoing resolution was duly moved by Councilor Matters and seconded by Councilor McHugh and brought to a vote resulting as follows: Councilor R. Matters VOTED: Councilor J. McHugh VOTED: Supervisor J. Conway VOTED: Councilor H. Kennedy VOTED: Councilor L. Koenig VOTED: 238-2026 A Resolution Authorizing the Additional Funding for Construction Inspection for the Railroad Ave Sewer Line Extension Project WHEREAS, the Town Board approved a task order with H.V. LaBarba via Resolution 237-2025 for an amount of $18,000.00; and WHEREAS, H.V. LaBarba contacted the Commissioner of Public Works to address a concern that the original estimate for work included 100 hrs for 2 ½ weeks of anticipated construction of new sanitary sewer on Railroad Ave by American Evergreen at an estimated cost of $18,000. Due to deliberate contractor efforts and the presence of subsoil rock the length of construction time extended the onsite inspection hours by an additional 90 hours, thus incurring an additional fee of $13,500; WHEREAS, the Director of Finance confirms the use of Sewer Fund Balance will be necessary to cover the overage in the amount of $13,500; now, therefore, be it RESOLVED, that the Town Board does hereby approve the use of Sewer Fund Balance in the amount of $13,500 to 07.8120.4 Sanitary Sewer to cover the additional cost of construction inspection by HV Labarba. The foregoing resolution was duly moved by Councilor Kennedy and seconded by Councilor Matters and brought to a vote resulting as follows: Councilor H. Kennedy VOTED: Councilor R. Matters VOTED: Supervisor J. Conway VOTED: Councilor J. McHugh VOTED: Councilor L. Koenig VOTED: 239-2026 A Resolution Authorizing the Rock Contingency for the Railroad Ave Sewer Main Extension Project WHEREAS, the Town Board authorized the contract with American Evergreen for the Railroad Ave Sewer Main Extension project for a construction amount of $142,000 in Resolution 100-2026; and 5 WHEREAS, the bid and resolution identified the cost of rock removal should the contractor encounter rock while digging at the amount of $200 per cubic yard; and WHEREAS, a contingency amount was not built into the total price, outside of identifying the rock removal at $200/cy; and WHEREAS, American Evergreen has submitted a final payment request that includes 82 cubic yards of rock at a total of $16,400 in addition to the $142,000.00 for a project total of $158,400.00; and WHEREAS, Town Designated Engineer on this project, H.V. LaBarba, has confirmed that this amount of rock was removed and the cause of some delay on the project and has signed off on the contingency amount, recommending the Commissioner to pay the amount; and WHEREAS, the Director of Finance confirms the use of Sewer Fund Balance will be necessary to cover the overage in the amount of $16,400; now, therefore, be it RESOLVED, that the Town Board does hereby authorize the rock contingency payment in the amount of $16,400 to American Evergreen bringing the project total to $158,400. The foregoing resolution was duly moved by Councilor McHugh and seconded by Councilor Koenig and brought to a vote resulting as follows: Councilor J. McHugh VOTED: Councilor L. Koenig VOTED: Supervisor J. Conway VOTED: Councilor H. Kennedy VOTED: Councilor R. Matters VOTED: 240-2026 A Resolution Accepting the Insurance Recovery and Allocating the Funds to Repair of Damage to the Morgan Road Guiderail WHEREAS, On June 26, 2026 an incident occurred on Morgan Road that resulted in the damage to the Guiderail; and WHEREAS, the incident information, pictures and repair quote were submitted to the Town’s Insurance Company resulting in the Town receiving an Insurance Recovery check in the amount of $13,998.00 for the cost of repair; and WHEREAS, the Commissioner of Public Works is requesting the Insurance Recovery check be transferred to the General Repairs line for Guiderail repairs to allow the repairs to be completed; and WHEREAS, the Town uses Town & Country Bridge and Rail (TCBR) for all guiderail repairs and installation under Rensselaer County Contract (RFB 26-07: Guide Railing Installation); and WHEREAS, the Director of Finance confirms that the Insurance Recovery check has been deposited into 2.2680 -Insurance Recovery- and a budget amendment is needed to account 02.5110.4-General Repairs- in the amount $13,998 pay for the repair of the guiderail; now, therefore, be it RESOLVED, that the Town Board does hereby accept the Insurance Recovery and authorizes the budget amendment to 02.5110.4 – General Repairs to cover the cost of repair; and be it further, RESOLVED, that the Town Board hereby approves the Commissioner to schedule the guiderail repair on Morgan Road. 6 The foregoing resolution was duly moved by Councilor Koenig and seconded by Supervisor Conway and brought to a vote resulting as follows: Councilor L. Koenig VOTED: Supervisor J. Conway VOTED: Councilor H. Kennedy VOTED: Councilor R. Matters VOTED: Councilor J. McHugh VOTED: 241-2026 A Resolution to Set the Transfer Station Rates for 2027 WHEREAS, it is required to establish policies and rates for the use of the East Greenbush Transfer Station on an annual basis; and WHEREAS, the Commissioner of Public Works, Deputy Commissioner of Public Works and Transfer Station personnel met and discussed various fees during the review along with increase in costs charged to the Town by the City of Albany for Landfill Tip Fees, as well as other disposal fees; and WHEREAS, the City of Albany Landfill is facing critical infrastructure issues that could pose a threat to the current processes that the Town of East Greenbush is accustomed to and as a result, we will be meeting with officials in the Capital Region Solid Waste Management Planning Unit (aka Capital Region Recycling Partnership or CRRP) to remain up to date on the plans and processes that will be effective by 2028; and WHEREAS, the annual cost of a Transfer Station permit and punch cards will have a slight increase in 2027; and WHEREAS, the Director of Finance confirms that this resolution supports the FYE 2027 Budget; now, therefore, be it RESOLVED, that the proposed policies and rates for 2027 be made effective for the year 2027. The foregoing resolution was duly moved by Councilor Kennedy and seconded by Councilor Koenig and brought to a vote resulting as follows: Councilor H. Kennedy VOTED: Councilor L. Koenig VOTED: Supervisor J. Conway VOTED: Councilor R. Matters VOTED: Councilor J. McHugh VOTED: 242-2026 A Resolution Approving the Adoption of the Annual Budget for Fiscal Year 2027 WHEREAS, pursuant to New York Town Law § 106, subd. 2, the East Greenbush Town Supervisor duly filed a Tentative Budget and budget message in the Office of the Town Clerk on September 30, 2026 (referred to hereinafter as the “Tentative Budget”); and WHEREAS, the Tentative Budget provided for a 1.97% increase in the Town’s Real Property Tax Levy for fiscal year 2027; and WHEREAS, pursuant to New York Town Law § 106, subd. 4, the East Greenbush Town Board, at the scheduled Town Board meeting held on October 28, 2026 duly approved a 7 Preliminary Budget which was filed in the office of the Town Clerk on October 27, 2026 (referred to hereinafter as the “Preliminary Budget”); and WHEREAS, pursuant to New York Town Law § 108, the East Greenbush Town Board duly conducted a public hearing on November 5, 2026 on the Preliminary Budget; and WHEREAS, the Director of Finance confirms that this resolution will not have a material impact on the Town’s finances because appropriations are matched to revenue and fund balance; and WHEREAS, the final Adopted Budget will have the attachments of the Analysis of Fund Balance Page and Assessor’s Exemption Report; now, therefore, be it RESOLVED, that, pursuant to New York Town Law § 109, subd. 1, the Preliminary Budget be, and the same hereby is, duly adopted as the Annual Budget for fiscal year 2027 (referred to hereinafter as the “Adopted Budget”); and be it further RESOLVED, that the Town Clerk shall cause a copy of the Adopted Budget to be duly filed in her office, forthwith, following receipt thereof from the Director of Finance; and be it further RESOLVED, that, pursuant to New York Town Law § 109, subd. 3, the Supervisor, Director of Finance, Comptroller, Receiver of Taxes, and Assessor take all respective action required and/or appropriate relative to the implementation of the Adopted Budget. The foregoing resolution was duly moved by Supervisor Conway and seconded by Councilor Kennedy and brought to a vote resulting as follows: Supervisor J. Conway VOTED: Councilor H. Kennedy VOTED: Councilor R. Matters VOTED: Councilor J. McHugh VOTED: Councilor L. Koenig VOTED: 243-2026 A Resolution to Set the Capital Costs and Operation and Maintenance Costs for the Consolidated General Water District and Consolidated General Sewer District in 2027 WHEREAS, the Town Board wishes to ensure the fiscal stability of the Consolidated General Water District and Consolidated General Sewer District in 2027 and beyond; and WHEREAS, funding for the Consolidated General Water and Consolidated General Sewer District must cover capital costs as well as operation and maintenance costs; and WHEREAS, capital costs will be covered by the cost per unit of assessment charged on the annual tax bill and operation and maintenance costs will be funded by user rates; and WHEREAS, a public hearing was held on the 2027 water and sewer rates on November 5, 2026 and all comments were heard; and WHEREAS, the Director of Finance confirms that this resolution will not have a material impact on the Town’s finances; now, therefore, be it RESOLVED, that payment of capital costs for the Town of East Greenbush Consolidated General Water District and Consolidated General Sewer District for the year 8 January 1, 2027 to December 31, 2027 shall be based upon a Unit of Assessment as set forth in Schedule A, attached hereto and made a part hereof; and be it further RESOLVED, that the payment of capital costs and debt service, and operation and maintenance expenses for the Town of East Greenbush Consolidated General Water District for the year January 1, 2027 to December 31, 2027 shall be as follows: Water Rate Type Water Debt Units Water Tax Levy East Greenbush Users Out of Town Users 2027 Units in the District Per Debt Unit Cost Per 100 Cubic Feet 14,099 37.03 $ 4.48 Per 1,000 Gallons $ 5.99 Per 100 Cubic Feet Per 1,000 Gallons $ 6.72 $ 8.98 and be it further RESOLVED, that the payment of capital costs and debt service, and operation and maintenance expenses for the Town of East Greenbush Consolidated General Sewer District for the year January 1, 2027 to December 31, 2027 shall be as follows: Debt Units Sewer Tax Levy East Greenbush Users Out of Town Users Sewer Rate Type

text: TOWN OF EAST GREENBUSH PLANNING BOARD TOWN HALL, 225 COLUMBIA TURNPIKE, RENSSELAER, NY 12144 | (518) 477-2005 | FAX (518) 477-2386 MEETING AGENDA NOVEMBER 18, 2026 I. 7:00PM CALL TO ORDER/DETERMINATION OF QUORUM: Meeting is to be held in the Community Room at Town Hall. II. PUBLIC HEARINGS: (26-14) Patroon Place – 550 Third Avenue Extension – Major Site Plan/Special Use Permit (26-22) Martin Electric – 164 Columbia Turnpike – Site Plan Modification/Special Use Permit III. OLD BUSINESS: (23-17) Seaboard Solar – Miller Road Solar, LLC – 465 Miller Road – Major Site Plan/SUP Special Use Permit Renewal (23-17a) Seaboard Solar – Miller Road Solar West, LLC – 465 Miller Road – Major Site Plan/SUP Special Use Permit Renewal (25-13) PetroCAS, LLC – 35-45 Discovery Drive – Major Site Plan/Lot Line Adjustment Discussion – Review for Recommendation to the Town Board and LLA Approval (26-14) Patroon Place – 550 Third Avenue Extension – Major Site Plan/Special Use Permit Special Use Permit Review – Review for Recommendation to the Town Board (26-22) Martin Electric – 164 Columbia Turnpike – Site Plan Modification/Special Use Permit Special Use Permit Review IV. REVIEW & APPROVAL OF MEETING MINUTES: October 28, 2026 meeting minutes *To view application materials, use this link: https://eastgreenbush.org/departments/planning___zoning/projects.php Town of East Greenbush PLANNING BOARD In the matter by: Miller Road Solar, LLC For a Special Use Permit Renewal Resolution and Final Decision of Planning Board File No. 23-17 Whereas, an application has been filed by Miller Road Solar, LLC for the construction and operation of a Large-Scale Solar Energy System located at Miller Rd (TAX ID #167.-4-36), East Greenbush, NY 12061; and Whereas, the Planning Board granted conditional approval of the Special Use Permit for this use on May 22, 2024, with the condition that the applicant renew the Special Use Permit before May 22, 2026, to ensure compliance with the conditions of approval; and Whereas, the applicant has timely requested renewal of the Special Use Permit and has provided documentation to demonstrate compliance with the conditions set forth in the original resolution; and Whereas, the Planning Board has reviewed all relevant materials and documents provided by the applicant and determined that the operation has been in compliance with all required conditions and regulations; and Whereas, the Planning Board has conducted a review of the application for renewal, including a review of the SEQRA determination made during the original approval, and affirms that there are no significant new environmental impacts to be considered; and Whereas, the Planning Board finds that the conditions outlined in the original resolution remain valid and applicable; and now, therefore, be it, Resolution and Final Decision of Planning Board: Appeal No. 23-17 Resolved, That the Special Use Permit for a Large-Scale Solar Energy System, Tier 2 for the subject property located on Miller Road (TAX ID #167.-4-36), East Greenbush, NY 12061, is hereby renewed with the following conditions: 1. The applicant must comply with all local, State, and Federal laws. 2. The applicant must continue to comply with the site plan and all conditions associated with the site plan approved by the Town Board. 3. The Special Use Permit renewal is subject to the applicant's continued compliance with the conditions outlined in the original resolution dated May 22, 2024. 4. Satisfying outstanding technical details as determined by this Planning Board and by the Town Planning and Zoning Department 5. This Special Use Permit remains valid until August 31, 2027 unless there is a material change to the use or site plan that requires further Planning Board and/or Town Board review. TOWN OF EAST GREENBUSH PLANNING BOARD By: ___ Matt Mastin, Chairperson Dated: , 2026 Town of East Greenbush PLANNING BOARD In the matter by: Miller Road Solar West, LLC For a Special Use Permit Renewal Resolution and Final Decision of Planning Board File No. 23-17 Whereas, an application has been filed by Miller Road Solar West, LLC for the construction and operation of a Large-Scale Solar Energy System located at Miller Rd (TAX ID #167.-4-36), East Greenbush, NY 12061; and Whereas, the Planning Board granted conditional approval of the Special Use Permit for this use on May 22, 2024, with the condition that the applicant renew the Special Use Permit before May 22, 2026, to ensure compliance with the conditions of approval; and Whereas, the applicant has timely requested renewal of the Special Use Permit and has provided documentation to demonstrate compliance with the conditions set forth in the original resolution; and Whereas, the Planning Board has reviewed all relevant materials and documents provided by the applicant and determined that the operation has been in compliance with all required conditions and regulations; and Whereas, the Planning Board has conducted a review of the application for renewal, including a review of the SEQRA determination made during the original approval, and affirms that there are no significant new environmental impacts to be considered; and Whereas, the Planning Board finds that the conditions outlined in the original resolution remain valid and applicable; and now, therefore, be it, Resolution and Final Decision of Planning Board: Appeal No. 23-17a Resolved, That the Special Use Permit for a Large-Scale Solar Energy System, Tier 2 for the subject property located on Miller Road (TAX ID #167.-4-36), East Greenbush, NY 12061, is hereby renewed with the following conditions: 1. The applicant must comply with all local, State, and Federal laws. 2. The applicant must continue to comply with the site plan and all conditions associated with the site plan approved by the Town Board. 3. The Special Use Permit renewal is subject to the applicant's continued compliance with the conditions outlined in the original resolution dated May 22, 2024. 4. Satisfying outstanding technical details as determined by this Planning Board and by the Town Planning and Zoning Department 5. This Special Use Permit remains valid until August 31, 2026, unless there is a material change to the use or site plan that requires further Planning Board and/or Town Board review. TOWN OF EAST GREENBUSH PLANNING BOARD By: ___ Matt Mastin, Chairperson Dated: , 2026 PETROCAS, LLC LOT LINE ADJUSTMENT NOVEMBER 18, 2026 MOTION for SKETCH PLAT CLASSIFICATION (25-13) MOTION: A motion was made by Chairman Mastin as follows: The Town of East Greenbush Planning Board hereby classifies the action as a lot line adjustment under the Town’s Land Subdivision Regulations, Article IV, Section 2. MOTION for FINAL APPROVAL (25-13) MOTION: A motion was made by Chairman Mastin as follows: The Town of East Greenbush Planning Board hereby accepts the sketch plat and grants final approval of the proposed Lot Line Adjustment prepared by Lansing Engineering and dated May 21, 2026, subject to the following: - Satisfying outstanding technical details as determined by this Planning Board and by the Town Planning and Zoning Department; and - The approval of the Major Site Plan by the Town Board - All remaining fees are paid to the Town. TOWN OF EAST GREENBUSH TOWN PLANNING BOARD RESOLUTION A Resolution to Recommend that the Town Board of the Town of East Greenbush Issue an Approval of the Major Site Plan for the Integrated Liner Technologies Project (#25-13) MOTION: A motion was made by Chairman Mastin as follows: WHEREAS, the Town of East Greenbush Planning Board (the “Planning Board”) has received a Major Site Plan application submitted by Lansing Engineering on behalf of PetroCAS, LLC, involving an addition to the existing Integrated Liner Technologies facility at 35–45 Discovery Drive, Tax Map Nos. 155.-1-4.23 and 155.-1-4.24 (the “Project”); and WHEREAS, the Project was initially proposed as an approximately 53,283-square-foot addition and has since been reduced to approximately 48,325 square feet, together with related parking, four (4) additional loading docks, internal access drives, utilities, grading, stormwater management, landscaping, and consolidation of the two parcels into one approximately 11.77-acre parcel; and WHEREAS, the Project is located in the Research, Design & Technology (RDT) District, which permits light industrial and research and development uses, and is subject to the applicable dimensional, parking, and site-plan requirements of the Town’s Comprehensive Zoning Law; and WHEREAS, on September 17, 2025, the Town Board adopted Resolution No. 173-2025 initiating coordinated review pursuant to the State Environmental Quality Review Act (“SEQRA”), and on August 19, 2026, adopted Resolution No. 175-2026 issuing a Negative Declaration for the Project; and WHEREAS, the Planning Board considered the revised Project at its October 14, 2026 meeting, including proposed additional parking, loading facilities, stormwater management, and avoidance of identified potential wetland areas; and WHEREAS, Stantec Consulting Services Inc., the Town Designated Engineer (“TDE”) assigned to the Project, issued technical review comments dated October 21, 2026, and Lansing Engineering thereafter submitted revised plans and a November 6, 2026 comment-response letter addressing the identified items; and WHEREAS, the Planning Board understands that a separate lot line adjustment application is being considered for the consolidation of the two Project parcels and that the proposed Major Site Plan remains subject to completion of all necessary zoning, engineering, and agency reviews; and WHEREAS, the Planning Board has considered the information submitted to date and finds the proposed expansion generally appropriate for consideration by the Town Board, provided that the outstanding technical and zoning matters identified below are satisfactorily resolved; and WHEREAS, the ZBA granted the requested Variance for front yard parking on September 9, 2025; and now, therefore, be it RESOLVED, that the Planning Board hereby recommends that the Town Board consider granting Major Site Plan Approval for the PetroCAS, LLC / Integrated Liner Technologies Project at 35-45 Discovery Drive (PZD No. 25-13), subject to confirmation of the items identified in Conditions 1-3 before final Town Board action and the remaining applicable conditions of approval: 1. Prior to final Town Board site-plan approval, Stantec shall review the November 6, 2026 revised submission and provide written confirmation that its October 21, 2026 comments have been satisfactorily addressed or identify any specific remaining items to be incorporated into the final approval and plan set. 2. Prior to final Town Board site-plan approval, the applicant shall provide a verified zoning and parking compliance table for the consolidated parcel, including RDT area and bulk standards, maximum lot coverage, building setbacks, maximum-shift employee parking calculations, and the applicability and scope of the previously granted front-yard parking area variance. Any additional required zoning relief shall be obtained. 3. Prior to final Town Board site-plan approval, the applicant shall provide confirmation from the responsible Fire Official regarding adequate fire apparatus access, including access to the rear and west sides of the addition, or revise the plans to address any resulting comments. 4. The related lot line adjustment shall receive separate Planning Board approval and all required filing or recording shall be completed prior to issuance of building permits dependent upon the consolidated parcel configuration. 5. Prior to land disturbance, the applicant shall submit a final signed SWPPP and all required construction stormwater filings and approvals, incorporating final TDE and Town MS4 comments. Wetland protection fencing, reinforced erosion and sediment controls, and approved construction staging shall be installed and maintained in accordance with the approved plans. 6. The applicant shall coordinate with the Town regarding an enforceable stormwater operation and maintenance agreement for permanent stormwater management facilities, to be executed before issuance of a Certificate of Occupancy or as otherwise required by the Town. 7. The parking, truck access, loading areas, landscaping, screening, snow storage, site lighting, and other improvements shall be constructed and maintained substantially as shown on the final approved plans. Lighting shall meet applicable Town standards and minimize spillover onto neighboring properties. 8. Prior to issuance of building permits, the final revised plan set shall incorporate outstanding Town and TDE requirements, be approved by the appropriate Town officials, and bear the signatures required by the Town’s procedures. 9. The applicant shall obtain required permits, satisfy applicable agency requirements, and pay all outstanding application, escrow, inspection, and other required Town fees before the applicable permit or authorization is issued. 10. Prior to issuance of a Certificate of Occupancy, the applicant shall provide required record/asbuilt documentation and engineer certification of substantially conforming construction, subject to review and acceptance by the Town and/or TDE. 11. Any material modification to the approved plans or proposed use shall be submitted for review and approval by the appropriate Town board or official before implementation. and be it further RESOLVED, that this recommendation does not constitute final Major Site Plan approval, lot line adjustment approval, a building permit, or authorization to commence construction; final approval remains within the jurisdiction of the Town Board and other applicable agencies. Resolution and Final Decision of Planning Board: PZD No. 26-14 Town of East Greenbush PLANNING BOARD In the matter by: Patroon Place For a Special Use Permit Resolution and Final Decision of Planning Board File No. 26-14 Whereas, Michael Moscatiello has submitted an application for a Major Site Plan and Special Use Permit for property located at 550 Third Avenue Extension, Rensselaer, New York, identified as Tax Map No. 144.-4-49, within the Regional Commercial (RC) District (the “Property”); and Whereas, the application proposes construction of an approximately 160-foot by 70-foot, 11,200-squarefoot detached building containing eight (8) individually leased garage-bay storage units at the rear of the existing site, together with associated parking and circulation modifications, lighting, landscaping, screening, grading, stormwater management, and related site improvements; and Whereas, the proposed use is classified as “Storage; self-storage rental facility,” which is a Special Permit Use in the RC District pursuant to Section 2.7.4(C) of the Town of East Greenbush Comprehensive Zoning Law, subject to the general standards set forth in Section 3.11.1(A) and all other applicable requirements of the Comprehensive Zoning Law; and Whereas, the applicant has represented that the eight (8) proposed units will be used for storage purposes, including storage associated with small contractor or commercial tenants, and that the proposal does not include active contractor-shop operations, manufacturing or fabrication, vehicle repair, retail sales, residential occupancy, or outdoor storage as part of the Special Use Permit request; and Whereas, the existing approximately 4,372-square-foot commercial building along Third Avenue Extension will remain, with no physical or operational changes to that building or to the existing site access points proposed as part of this application; and Whereas, the Town Board, by Resolution No. 147-2026 dated July 15, 2026, initiated coordinated review under the State Environmental Quality Review Act (“SEQRA”), and following review of the revised Project scope issued a Negative Declaration by Resolution No. 192-2026 on September 16, 2026, determining that the Project will not result in any significant adverse environmental impacts; and Whereas, the proposed site configuration exceeds the maximum lot coverage permitted in the RC District, and the Zoning Board of Appeals granted the required area variance for lot coverage on October 14, 2026; and Whereas, notice of the Special Use Permit public hearing was duly published in The Record on November 7, 2026, and notice was provided to property owners within two hundred (200) feet and to applicable agencies in accordance with the Comprehensive Zoning Law; and Whereas, the Planning Board conducted a duly noticed public hearing on November 18, 2026, at which interested persons were afforded an opportunity to be heard, and the Planning Board has considered the statements, written submissions, exhibits, and other materials received as part of the hearing record; and Whereas, the Planning Board has reviewed the application, site plans, applicant representations, the Town Board’s SEQRA determination, the Zoning Board of Appeals determination, and the applicable Special Use Permit standards of the Comprehensive Zoning Law; now, therefore, be it Resolution and Final Decision of Planning Board: PZD No. 26-14 Resolved, that the Planning Board makes the following findings under Section 3.11.1(A) of the Comprehensive Zoning Law: 1. The location and size of the proposed self-storage rental facility, the nature and intensity of the operations involved, the size of the site in relation to the use, and the location of the site with respect to existing streets providing access are in harmony with the orderly development of the RC District. The proposed building is located to the rear of an existing commercial building on an already developed commercial parcel and will utilize the site’s existing access points. 2. The location, nature, and height of the proposed storage building, together with the nature and intensity of the approved storage operations, will not discourage the appropriate development and use of adjacent land and buildings or impair the value thereof, subject to implementation and maintenance of the approved landscaping, screening, architectural treatment, and other site-plan improvements. 3. The traffic accessways serving the proposed use are adequate but not excessive in number and are adequate in width, grade, alignment, and visibility for the approved use. No new curb cuts are proposed, and the Project will continue to use the existing site access points, subject to the circulation and emergency-access requirements of the final approved Major Site Plan. 4. Adequate provision for safe and accessible off-street parking and loading can be provided on the Property. Parking, loading, maneuvering, and access associated with the storage units shall occur only within the areas shown on the final approved Major Site Plan and shall not obstruct internal circulation or emergency access. 5. Parking and service areas shall be screened from adjacent residential properties and streets to the extent required by the Comprehensive Zoning Law, and the general landscaping of the site shall be consistent with the approved Major Site Plan. Existing mature vegetation shall be preserved to the maximum extent practicable and supplemented with approved landscaping and screening. 6. The character and appearance of the proposed self-storage use and storage building will be in general harmony with the surrounding commercial area and will not be more objectionable to nearby properties by reason of noise, fumes, vibration, lighting, or other operational impacts than permitted uses in the district. This finding is based upon the limited storage use represented by the applicant and the conditions of this approval prohibiting active contractor-shop operations, vehicle repair, manufacturing or fabrication, … The approval does not authorize a battery energy storage system. C OF 2026 A LOCAL LAW TO AMEND THE SUPPLEMENTARY REGULATIONS OF CHAPTER 235 OF THE CODE OF THE TOWN OF MARCELLUS TO ADD NEW REGULATIONS FOR BATTERY ENERGY STORAGE SYSTEMS IN THE TOWN OF MARCELLUS BE IT ENACTED by the Town Board of the Town of Marcellus as follows: SECTION 1. LEGISLATIVE PURPOSE AND INTENT. The purpose of this Local Law is to enact battery energy storage system regulations in the Town of Marcellus. The Town Board of the Town of Marcellus makes the following findings, which are cumulative and interrelated and shall be liberally construed. Throughout New York State, shortsighted and haphazard planning has frequently resulted in the creation or exacerbation of industries which adversely impact public health and quality of life, cause proliferation of pollution, compromise aesthetics, and degrade community character, including the solar industry and associated battery energy storage: A. Battery energy storage systems have increased significantly in number throughout the State and country and without careful planning, they can be sited without sufficient regard for their impact on the health, welfare, and safety of residents; The Town of Marcellus is a suburban rural community with a diverse landscape consisting of extensive water frontage, a significant amount of wetlands, and sensitive soils; The Town of Marcellus has a significant agricultural community supporting various agricultural uses; ; If not properly regulated, installation of battery energy storage systems can create drainage problems through erosion and lack of sediment control for facility and access roads and can harm farmland and wetlands through improper construction methods; Battery energy storage systems, when improperly sited, are known to adversely affect property values and cause economic hardship to property owners; Battery energy storage systems may be significant sources of noise, including infrasound, that, if unregulated, can negatively affect quiet enjoyment of the area, properties, and the health and quality of life of residents; Construction of battery energy storage systems can create traffic problems and can cause damage to local roads and infrastructure due to the weight of the units; Battery energy storage systems have the potential to cause electromagnetic interference with various types of communications; I. Battery energy storage systems need to be regulated for removal when no longer utilized. It is incumbent upon the Town of Marcellus to ensure that funding for removal is secured as part of the permitting process; (1) As of the date of enactment of this Law, the overwhelming majority of utility- or grid-scale battery energy storage systems in the United States, which are classified as “Tier 3” herein, utilize lithium-ion cells. While lithium-ion battery technology offers numerous advantages in terms of longevity, energy density, and weight, it has numerous drawbacks as well, many of which are of concern to the Town Board, including but not limited to the following: lithium-ion batteries utilize flammable electrolytes rather than the aqueous (water-based) electrolytes found in older battery technologies such as lead-acid and nickel-metal hydride; (2) Lithium-ion batteries are particularly vulnerable to a condition known as “thermal runaway” whereby heat is generated at a higher rate than it can be dissipated. If a cell- specific critical temperature is reached, the internal cell structure-Can break down and the flammable electrolyte generates a flammable gas. If the internal pressure within the cell exceeds the mechanical strength of the battery housing, the housing may rupture. Alternatively, if the pressure exceeds a pre-set limit, a safety valve may open. In either case, a situation known as an “off-gas” event has occurred, and if an ignition source is present, the gaseous electrolyte may ignite; LS (3) Ignition of gaseous electrolyte or the heat generated by the thermal runaway itself can heat adjacent cells above their critical temperatures, resulting in a cascading thermal runaway. Thus, a failure in a single cell failure may propagate and cause a catastrophic event. involving the entire system; va (4) Off-gas events can release substantial amounts of electrolyte and combustion gases. Off- gases from lithium-ion batferies are extremely toxic and can contain mixtures of carbon monoxide, hydrogen, ethylene, methane, ethane, benzene, hydrogen fluoride, hydrogen chloride, and hydrogen cyanide, depending on the battery type. Hydrogen fluoride forms hydrofluoric acid ugon contact with water, including water vapor in the air and moisture in the lungs and on the eyes. Hydrofluoric acid is highly corrosive and can cause chemical burns and blizdness and, in addition, is a powerful contact poison that is readily absorbed through the skin, eyes, and lungs and can cause cardiac arrest. Hydrogen chloride forms hydrochloric acid upon contact with water, including water vapor in the air and moisture in te lungs and on the eyes. Hydrochloric acid is corrosive and can cause chemical burns omthe skin, respiratory tract, and eyes, and in severe cases can cause permanent eye damage and death; and (5) If off-gas accumulates within a space, there is a high risk of instantaneous ignition. The pressure from the resulting deflagration can rupture the structure: J. In the event of a thermal runaway, other battery failure, or a conventional fire that spreads to the batteries, the foregoing constitute a serious danger to first responders, passers-by, and persons on nearby properties. They also constitute a serious environmental hazard; 2 K. Due to the foregoing risks, this Local Law contains regulations requiring passive and active fire protection, explosion prevention, and other measures to mitigate the serious risks inherent to battery energy storage systems. However, no policy, procedure, or measure can provide complete safety or an absolute guarantee against a catastrophic event. Accordingly, strict rules and regulations regarding the construction, operation, and placement of battery energy storage systems ‘are appropriate; and when considering the construction and maintenance of large-scale systems, appropriate weight and consideration should be given to numerous factors, including but not limited to the following: (1) The proximity of the proposed system to residential areas, schools, environmental resources including but not limited to wetlands, rivers, lakes, streams, and creeks; (2) The relative distress and disruption caused to the community; (3) The actual necessity for such facility given energy production “in the area and region, including but not limited to clean energy production; . (4) Past and present stresses and disruption imposed upon an area due to all types of energy production; (5) Alternatives to the proposed facility, including focation in other areas, location in areas where demand is greater; and a (6) The need to balance the burden upon the community with the potential benefits that the community may enjoy if the facility.is approved. In light of the foregoing, the Town Board finds a need to properly site battery energy storage systems within the boundaries of the Town to protect residential, business areas, and other land uses, to preserve the overall beauty, nature and vharacter of the Town, to promote the effective and efficient use of battery energy resources, and to protect the health, safety and general welfare of the citizens of the Town. This Local Law is adopted-to do so with the following objectives: A. To provide a regtlatory scheme for the designation of properties suitable for the location, construction and operation of battery energy storage systems; - To ensure compatible land uses in the vicinity of the areas affected by battery energy storage systems; To mitigate the impacts of battery energy storage systems on environmental resources such as important agricultural lands, forests, wildlife, and other protected resources; To ensure appropriate siting of battery energy storage systems in accordance with the Town’s Comprehensive Plan, and other Town policy and-land use goals: To create synergy between battery energy storage system development and: 3 (1) Promotion and management of new development in the Town which protects resources and the Town’s unique identity; (2) General growth of the Town, which shall occur ina manner that preserves the quality of life and character of the community; (3) Preservation and enhancement of the character of existing neighborhoods; (4) Preservation and protection of natural resources and farmland, and support for the agricultural economy; and (5) The availability of public facilities, infrastructure, and services that adequately serve the present and future needs of the Town. / SECTION 2. AUTHORITY. This Local Law is adopted pursuant to the New York State Constitution, Article IX, Section 2(c)(6), (10); New York Statute of Local Governments, Section 10(1), (7); New York State Town Law Sections 261-263; and Municipal Home Rule Law Section 10; all which authorize the Town to adopt zoning provisions that advance and protect the health, safety and welfare of the community. SECTION 3. AMENDMENT OF SECTION 235-26 (“SUPPLEMENTARY REGULATIONS”) OF CHAPTER 235 (“ZONING”) OF THE CODE OF THE TOWN OF MARCELLUS. . y Section 235-26, “Supplementary Regulations,” of Chapter 235, “Zoning,” of the Code of the Town of Marcellus shall be amended to add a new Subsection “N,” titled “Battery energy storage systems,” which shall read in its entirety as follows: “N. Battery energy storage systéms. (1) Definitions. Asjused in this section, the following terms shall have the meanings indicated: ANSI American National Standards Institute. BATTERY(/IES) A single cell or a group of cells connected together electrically in series, in parallel, or a combination of both, which can charge, discharge, and store energy electrochemically. For the purposes of this Subsection, batteries utilized in consumer products are excluded from these requirements. BATTERY ENERGY STORAGE MANAGEMENT SYSTEM An electronic supervisory system that protects energy storage systems from operating 4 outside their safe operating parameters and disconnects electrical power to the energy storage system or places it in a safe condition if potentially hazardous temperatures or other conditions are detected. One of the main functions of the BMS is to keep the cells operating within their designed operating parameters to prevent thermal runaway. BATTERY ENERGY STORAGE SYSTEM A collection of cells, assembled together, housed in a self-contained unit, or in a building that is constructed to meet specific standards related to industry and local fire codes, that is capable of storing energy in order to supply electrical energy to a building, a group of | buildings, and/or the electrical grid at a future time. A battery energy storage system is classified as a Tier 1, Tier 2, or Tier 3 battery energy storage system as follows: (a) Tier 1 Battery Energy Storage Systems include either: [1] Battery energy storage systems for one- to two-family residential dwellings within or outside the structure with an aggregate energy capacity that shall not exceed: i. 40 kWh within utility closets and storage or utility spaces: ii. 80 kWh in attached or detached garages and detached accessory structures: iii. 80 kWh on exterior walls; or SL iv. 80 kWh outdoors on the ground. [2] Other battery energy storage systems with an aggregate energy capacity less than or equal to the thresliold capacity listed’ in Table 1. (b) Tier 2 Battery Energy Storage Systems include battery energy storage systems that are not included in Tier 1, have an aggregate energy capacity greater than the threshold capacity listed in Tablet, and have an aggregate energy capacity less than 600 kWh. low batt 20 kWh Lead acid, alltypes 70 kWh Lithium, all types 20 kWh [Nickel cadmium (Ni-Cd) 70 kWh Nickel metal hydride (Ni-MH) 70 kWh Other battery technologies 10 kWh (c) Tier 3 Battery Energy Storage Systems include either: [1] Battery energy storage systems with an aggregate energy capacity greater than or equal to 600 kWh; or [2] Battery energy storage systems with more than one storage battery technology provided in a room or indoor area. 5

Box 1179 Southold, New York 11971 Fax (631) 765-6145 Telephone (631) 765-1800 www.southoldtownny.gov Office of the Town Clerk Town of Southold Agenda Final Southold Town Board November 17, 2026 6:00 PM POLICY: At the beginning of scheduled Town Board meetings, the attending public is encouraged to briefly address the Town Board relating to agenda resolutions prior to their enactment; the public will also be given time at the conclusion of the regularly scheduled business agenda to address the Board on any given topic. ONLINE ACCESS: The Tentative Agenda is generally available the Friday before the meeting. The video of the meeting is usually available to watch live during the meeting. Minutes with adopted resolutions are available 1 to 2 days after the meeting. A full copy of the minutes, agenda and meeting video can be viewed on the official Town of Southold website. If you would like help navigating the site, please feel free to call my office 631-765-1800. The meeting will be accessible in person and via Zoom and streamed live on the Town’s website. A recording of the meeting will also air on Channel 1310 and will be posted on the Town’s website. Instructions and link to attend the meeting will be available on the Town’s website or by calling the Town Clerk’s office at (631)765-1800. A telephone number will also be provided to allow members of the public to attend via telephone. Written comments and/or questions may also be submitted via email to the Town Clerk at denisn@southoldtownny.gov. Said comments and/or questions will be considered at the public hearing provided that they are submitted no later than 12:00 P.M. (Prevailing Time) on the day of the public hearing. Please check the meeting Agenda posted on the Town’s website for further instructions or for any changes to the instructions to access the public hearing, and for updated information. I.
